policy_conformance_independently_verifie.why: A 63% sharp-edge ratio could indicate blanket-sharpening, which would satisfy the FBX layer check while violating the smoothing policy.
policy_conformance_independently_verifie.method: Recompute the 30 degree dihedral rule directly from the OSM2World OBJ, per object, and compare with the sharp-edge count Blender recorded.

tile_10_9.delta_cause: Blender merges vertices by distance on OBJ import, which removes 2 duplicate edges relative to the raw OBJ topology

policy_conformance_independently_verifie.conclusion: The sharp-edge set matches an independent recomputation of the stated policy, and no sub-degree (coplanar) edge was hardened. Hard edges occur only at genuine corners, wall/roof intersections and boundaries.

smoothing_policy.principle: Smooth only where the surface is geometrically continuous; keep hard edges everywhere the surface actually turns.
hard_edges: vertical wall corners between adjacent wall faces
smooth_regions: coplanar wall faces of a single facade
coplanar roof faces within one roof plane
smoothing_policy.threshold_rationale: A building is a hard-edged object: walls are near-vertical planes meeting at roughly 90 degrees, and roof planes meet ridges at roughly 30 degrees or less. 30 degrees separates real geometry from the sub-degree wobble of a triangulated plane, so coplanar triangles stay smooth while real corners stay hard. This is a semantic choice about building geometry, deliberately independent of the 1e-12 m^2 degenerate-area fail-closed threshold.
smoothing_policy.not_a_warning_suppression: The warning is expected to disappear because the FBX now carries the information UE4 asks for. No log filtering, no import-setting change, and no MikkTSpace disablement is involved.
